answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with stake-weighted reputation that grows like a trellis: each agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and its reputation climbs only through verified work endorsed by counterparties. A fake identity starts with no trust and earns nectar slowly, one completed task at a time, while misbehavior slashes its deposit. This makes forgery expensive: an attacker must fund every fake, wait out a glacier-slow vesting period, and still lose the stake if any identity cheats, so creating thousands of Sybils costs far more than the fraud could ever return.
